annotationRationale: The main route identifies exhaustive, mutually exclusive successful beginnings and combines independent-roll probabilities. The reviewed alternative constructs a recursion from the remaining target. Recursion remains specific to that alternative.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Under the usual independent fair-die model, the successful prefixes are 3; 1,2; 2,1; and 1,1,1. Their disjoint probabilities sum to 49/216, agreeing with choice B and the key. A fourth-roll first hit is impossible. No statement or figure contradiction.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both shared methods from 2023_AMC_10A_Q07 were independently verified and retained: disjoint-hit-prefixes enumerates successful beginnings, while remaining-target-recursion builds probabilities from smaller remaining targets. The recursion is an accessible, genuinely different reusable approach. No useful supplied shared route was omitted.
review.annotationCheck: Probability addition and independent-event multiplication are appropriately assessed, with elementary fair-outcome probability as support. State recursion is correctly confined to the alternative method. The unequal probabilities of different-length prefixes make the former equal-outcome enumeration node unnecessary.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Positive rolls force a hit within three rolls. The four prefixes exhaust all compositions of 3 and are mutually exclusive. Their probabilities are 1/6,1/36,1/36,1/216; unrestricted later rolls introduce no further factor. The sum is 49/216.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The method accurately reuses amc/2023_AMC_10A_Q07#disjoint-hit-prefixes. Its shared reference and both inherited IDs, live-reference-2023_AMC_10A_Q07 and randommath-reference-2023_AMC_10A_Q07, are retained. The source-informed-original designation and project versus third-party credits are accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation establishes exhaustiveness, disjointness, independence, and why later rolls are unrestricted. These address the material difficulties in adding probabilities of prefixes of different lengths.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h141 correctly describes multiplying independent-roll probabilities, and cnm_h138 correctly describes adding disjoint cases.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: Both accepted native topics directly apply through independent-event multiplication and mutually exclusive probability addition.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The supplied S-CP.B.7 link applies through its disjoint-event special case only. No accepted US link is supplied for cnm_h141. The question's supporting 7.SP.C.7a link concerns the fair-face model, not the whole argument.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The two direct nodes match the actual derivation, and their assessed roles are appropriate.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The remaining target is sufficient because future rolls are independent. With p₀=1, disjoint first-roll cases give p₁=1/6, p₂=7/36, and p₃=49/216. Success or overshoot is decided within at most r rolls, so the finite four-roll experiment is correctly represented.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The method accurately reuses amc/2023_AMC_10A_Q07#remaining-target-recursion and retains its sole inherited reference, live-reference-2023_AMC_10A_Q07. It credits the project-developed recursion rather than claiming that the supplied LIVE enumeration itself presents the recurrence.

methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:recursive-counting-probability precisely captures the state construction and initial condition. cnm_h141 and cnm_h138 correctly capture transition multiplication and disjoint-case addition.
